conviction_note: Nothing decisive was found. The evidence is a set of small, mostly macro or peer read-throughs that roughly offset. On the negative side: a Nashville peer's (FBK) margin squeeze was sold, rates backed up sharply against FHN's rate-sensitive fixed-income and warehouse lines, and revenue and expenses are tracking the edge of the FY guide. On the positive side: no rate cuts plus a Fed hike, on an asset-sensitive balance sheet, and positioning that is not crowded with the stock already off 14%. FHN has sold 5 of its last 7 prints, which pulls p_up to 45 on abs 3.0. That gives a scaled -0.3 against a findings sum of -0.8. The two numbers agree in sign and differ only because p_up carries the uncertainty.
bar: Q3 2026 consensus EPS $0.52-0.53 and revenue ~$893M. Benzinga had $0.52 / $893.2M on 2026-10-06 (down from $0.53 / $892.9M on 2026-09-18) and Earnings Whispers has $0.53 / $893.4M, so two sources agree to within a cent: https://www.benzinga.com/quote/fhn/earnings-forecasts and https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/x/FHN. Company FY2026 guide, reiterated at Q2 on 2026-07-15: adjusted revenue ex deferred comp +3% to +7% on a $3.42B base; adjusted expenses ex deferred comp flat on $2.05B, excluding incentive pay on incremental countercyclical revenue; NCO 0.15-0.25%; CET1 ~10.5%; NIM mid-to-high 3.40s per a third-party summary. Source: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000036966/000003696626000143/a2q26earningsslides.htm. That guide assumed 25bp cuts in April and July 2026. Neither happened, and the Fed hiked on 2026-09-16.
positioning_check: Short interest was ~10.6M shares, 1.9 days to cover, at the 2026-08-14 settlement, down from 16.3M / 3.3 days on 2026-06-15 (FINRA via curvedtrading: https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/fhn/short-interest/). That is not a crowded short. Skew is null in the baseline: no 25-delta skew available, put/call OI 1.12, total OI only 2,867, and the ATM spread is 67% of mid, so the 4.91% implied move is indicative only. Tape: -5.98% over 20 days, -2.13% over 5 days, -14.2% off the 52-week high, $22.50 against Q1/Q2 buyback averages of $24.54 / $24.52. KRE fell from 74.05 (2026-09-15) to ~68.49 (2026-10-14), about -7.5%, while FHN fell from 24.47 to 22.50, about -8.1%, so the drawdown is sector-wide rather than idiosyncratic. Realised vol is 16% annualised.

findings.finding: FB Financial (FBK), a Nashville-headquartered Tennessee peer, released Q3 2026 at 06:17 ET on 2026-10-13. EPS was $1.20 GAAP / $1.21 adjusted, roughly in line with $1.19-1.21 consensus. NIM fell 12bp q/q to 3.83% on 'higher funding costs relative to earning asset yields' (cost of interest-bearing deposits 2.88% vs 2.81%), and mortgage banking income fell to $9.4M from $11.2M. FBK closed 52.95 -> 50.72 (-4.2%) on the day while KRE moved ~-0.7% (69.56 -> 69.06). This is the first same-footprint print since FHN last spoke, and the market sold deposit-cost margin compression in an in-line quarter. FHN guided 'deposit costs trend up slightly' and grew brokered deposits 47% to $7.8B in Q2.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (2026-07-15): NIM -3bp to 3.49% on brokered-deposit cost with an EPS beat of $0.54 vs $0.53, and the stock fell -3.03%. FHN sells a margin-down print even on a beat.
findings.why_not_priced: FHN fell only 1.3% (23.06 -> 22.77) on the day FBK fell 4.2%, so the market applied little of the read-through to FHN. That is partly correct: FHN is asset-sensitive (+1.9% NII per +100bp) while FBK's loan yields were flat. If the market had fully transferred FBK's reaction, FHN would have traded down in step on 10-13.
findings.independence: S&P Global (2026-07-23) on an extended deposit-cost squeeze into 2027: https://www.spglobal.com/market-intelligence/en/news-insights/research/2026/07/us-banks-brace-for-an-extended-deposit-cost-squeeze. Morgan Stanley (2026-07-06) expects deposit costs to rise in 2H26, with Southeast promotional CD rates 10-45bp above the Northeast: https://www.itiger.com/news/2649962091. These are proxies, not FHN numbers.

findings.finding: The FY2026 guide assumed 25bp Fed cuts in April and July 2026. None came: the range held at 3.50-3.75% through July, then the FOMC hiked 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on 2026-09-16 by a 12-0 vote. FHN's own Q1 disclosure puts the next-12-month NII sensitivity at +1.9% for +100bp and -2.6% for -100bp (Q2: -3.3% for -100bp). Short rates are therefore ~50-75bp above the plan's path for most of 2H26, which supports NII and NIM toward the upper half of 'mid-to-high 340s' and gives room to firm the revenue guide. Q2 NII (FTE) was $679M, up $9M q/q.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean precedent in the baseline. The guide was reiterated (not raised) at Q1 and Q2, with reactions of -0.33% and -3.03%.
findings.why_not_priced: The hike is public, so this is partly priced. What is not visible is whether FHN converts it into a raised NII or revenue outlook or loses it to deposit pricing, as FBK did. Consensus revenue rose only $0.3M between 09-18 and 10-06 ($892.9M -> $893.2M) and EPS was trimmed from $0.53 to $0.52, so analysts have not credited a rate tailwind.
findings.independence: FHN sensitivity: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000036966/000003696626000067/a1q26earningsslides.htm. The plan's rate assumption: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000036966/000003696626000143/a2q26earningsslides.htm. Shares the macro fact 'rates rose' with the next finding, but lands on a different line (NII up vs fixed income and warehouse down).

findings.finding: Treasury par yields rose in Q3 2026: 10-year 4.44% (06-30) -> 5.29% (09-30), +85bp; 2-year 4.14% -> 4.88%. CEO Jordan said at Barclays on 2026-09-15 that rates had backed up significantly, accelerating in Q3, and that mortgage warehouse had softened on higher rates and line utilization was drifting down. The rate backup weighs on lines where FHN is exposed. FHN Financial fixed-income ADR was already down 20% q/q in Q2 ($594k vs $742k; Q3 2025 was $771k), and a selloff historically curbs depository clients' securities buying. Warehouse balances soften, and AOCI hits tangible book (CET1 is unaffected as a sub-$100B Category IV filer).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: fixed income fell $7M q/q to $46M within a print that sold off -3.03%. No print in the baseline isolates this line.
findings.why_not_priced: The rates are public and the market knows them. What is not known is the size of the Q3 fixed-income ADR and the warehouse decline, which only the release shows. Net of the rest of the company, fixed income is ~5% of revenue: a $100k ADR drop is ~$6M a quarter against $893M. Countercyclical PPNR is 8% of the total.
findings.independence: Barclays summary (Quartr, 2026-09-15): https://quartr.com/events/first-horizon-corporation-fhn-barclays-24th-annual-global-financial-services-conference_3sp4maWq. ADR history: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000036966/000003696626000143/a2q26earningsslides.htm. Shares the 'rates rose' fact with the Fed-hike finding.

findings.finding: Guide arithmetic from the company's own numbers. 1H26 adjusted FTE revenue was $865M (Q1) + $890M (Q2) = $1,755M. The FY range of +3% to +7% on $3.42B ($3.52-3.66B) needs ~$885-950M a quarter in 2H, and the $893M Q3 consensus sits near the bottom. Adjusted expenses were $526M in Q2, against ~$512M a quarter implied by flat $2.05B (Q2 up $26M q/q on personnel, technology and marketing). The likely outcome is the revenue guide narrowed toward the low end and expenses at or above the flat line. Caveat: the guide base excludes deferred comp, and my 1H figure may include it, so the gap is approximate.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q3 2025 print (2025-10-15), when guidance and capital-use commentary dominated with CEO M&A remarks, moved -9.43%. Reiterated-guide prints moved -0.33% and -3.03%.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus at $893M already sits near the low end, so most of this is inside what the market expects. It is sized small because the residual risk is a formal narrowing or an expense overshoot that the consensus revision (-$0.01 EPS) only partly reflects.
findings.independence: Q2 figures: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000036966/000003696626000143/a2q2026earningsrelease.htm. Consensus: https://www.benzinga.com/quote/fhn/earnings-forecasts. This is an inference from company documents, not a stated company number.

findings.finding: After Q2, $665M of buyback authorization remained (Q1 $233M at $24.54, Q2 $100M at $24.52). The stock now trades at $22.50, ~8% below those averages, so any Q3/Q4 repurchase retires more shares a dollar. CET1 was 10.5%, at its ~10.5% target, so capacity is roughly earnings retained beyond growth and dividends.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 buybacks fell from $233M to $100M, and that print sold -3.03%. No print in the baseline is identifiable as a buyback surprise.
findings.why_not_priced: The Q3 pace is unknown until the release. A larger buyback at lower prices would show up as share-count shrinkage that consensus EPS ($0.52) may not carry, but with CET1 at target the upside is bounded.

findings.finding: At Barclays on 2026-09-15 (Quartr summary), management said Q3 deposit growth was strong, 'supported by incentives', CRE lending was rebounding, pipelines were strong but utilization was drifting down, and borrower sentiment was cautiously optimistic. That is a mid-quarter company statement. Deposits bought with incentives can replace brokered funding but cost margin.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 deposit growth of +$1.6B, much of it brokered, came with NIM -3bp and a -3.03% reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: This is a public webcast, so largely priced. What remains is the cost of the incentive-driven deposits, which is not quantified anywhere before the release. A third-party summary, not a transcript.
findings.independence: Shares the Barclays document with the rates-backup finding (that finding cites the warehouse and rates remarks; this one the deposit and CRE remarks).

findings.finding: Positioning is light and the stock is already de-rated into the print. It sits at $22.50, -14.2% off its 52-week high, -6% over 20 days and below the $24.5 buyback averages. Short interest fell to 10.6M shares / 1.9 days (2026-08-14) from 16.3M / 3.3 days in June, and the 2-day straddle prices ~4.9% against a 1.62% median historical reaction. FHN's 8% fall since 09-15 roughly matches KRE's 7.5%, so the de-rating is sector-wide and leaves less room for a sector-driven drop on an in-line quarter.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The baseline shows 2 of 7 prints up. The one large move (-9.43%, 2025-10-15) came after the stock had been strong, not de-rated.
findings.why_not_priced: Positioning is by definition in the price. This is filed as a mild offset to the negative read-throughs: a name already down with the sector carries less downside on in-line numbers. Short interest is the August settlement; later settlements were not found.
findings.independence: KRE closes from the Yahoo chart: https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/KRE?range=3mo&interval=1d

findings.finding: Big-bank credit read: Wells Fargo's Q3 2026 release (2026-10-13) showed the provision up 51% y/y to $1.03B and NCOs at 0.38% (0.34% in Q2), and CEO Scharf flagged 'higher interest rates, higher oil prices and persistent inflation' as risks to the economy. Higher-for-longer rates stress CRE, a known FHN exposure in the Southeast. FHN's Q2 NCOs were 0.20%, inside its 0.15-0.25% guide, and NPLs fell $75M to $531M.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No credit-driven FHN print in the baseline window. Q2 credit improved, and the stock still fell -3.03% on margin and expenses.
findings.why_not_priced: This is a proxy, and WFC's NPAs actually fell $585M q/q. FHN's own credit trend was improving in Q2, so this is sized near zero. It would only matter if FHN reports a CRE migration, for which no FHN-specific evidence was found.
findings.independence: FBK's Q3 2026 NCOs were only 0.04%, which points the other way: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001649749/000164974926000063/a3q26pressreleasetablesfor.htm

baseline_tension: There is no skew to agree or disagree with (null). The mild negative lean runs with the 20-day run-up (-6%), so it is partly priced. The sector-wide de-rating and the asset-sensitive rate tailwind cut against it, which is why p_up sits at 45, not lower.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (a finding inside what the company has guided goes toward 0): the guide-arithmetic finding moved from -0.4 to -0.3, because the $893M consensus already sits near the low end of the guided range.
Rule 1 (the reaction function): FHN sold 5 of 7 prints, including the Q2 2026 beat (-3.03%), so p_up moved from 46 to 45. Finding sizes were left alone.
Rule 5 (a peer print after the company last spoke is what has paid): the FBK finding was kept at -0.6. It was not enlarged, because FBK's rate sensitivity differs from FHN's.

Two-readings rule: the Fed-hike and rates-backup findings share one macro fact but land on different lines (NII vs fixed income and warehouse), so both stand, with the shared fact noted in independence.
Rule 6 (bar): sourced to two agreeing estimates plus the company guide, so no cap applied.
